mobile.welcome.title: Control your Minecraft servers from your phone
Control your Minecraft servers from your phone
mobile.welcome.lead: Your phone talks straight to your PC over Tailscale. Nothing goes through anyone else's servers.
The app connects directly to the agent over your tailnet. No cloud relay.
mobile.welcome.need_tailscale: First, put Tailscale on this phone and sign in with the same account as your PC.
Install Tailscale on this phone and join the same tailnet as the PC.
mobile.welcome.scan_hint: On your PC, open the dashboard's App settings and find Open on your phone.
Dashboard: Agent settings > Phone pairing code.

mobile.pair.error_not_https: The app only connects with https, which keeps the connection private.
mobile.pair.error_bad_code: This code is damaged. Scan it again from the dashboard's App settings.

mobile.pair.too_old: The app on your PC is too old for this phone app. Update it on the PC from Settings, then try again.

mobile.pair.too_new: The app on your PC is newer than this phone app. Update the phone app, then try again.
The agent's API version is newer than this app supports. Update the phone app.
mobile.pair.confirm_lead: Your phone doesn't know this PC's certificate yet. Check that this matches Certificate fingerprint under Open on your phone in the dashboard's App settings.
The certificate isn't trusted by this phone. Compare the SHA-256 with the dashboard's pairing panel.
mobile.pair.confirm_no_body: Don't connect. Something between your phone and your PC may be pretending to be it. Scan the code on the PC instead.
Possible interception. Pair with the QR code instead.

mobile.help.pairing_body: Put Tailscale on the phone and sign in with the same account as your PC. On the PC, open the dashboard's App settings and scan the code under Open on your phone with this app. The code holds the PC's address and how to recognise it; it has no password in it.
Both devices join the same tailnet. The pairing QR code carries host, port, certificate SHA-256 and API version, no credentials. The app pins that fingerprint.
mobile.help.unreachable_title: When the app can't reach your PC
mobile.help.unreachable_body: The PC may be asleep or off, the app on the PC may not be running, or this phone may not be on Tailscale. Open Tailscale on the phone and check it says Connected.
Check the host is awake, the agent service is running and Tailscale is connected on the phone.
mobile.help.certificate_title: When the app says the certificate changed
mobile.help.certificate_body: The PC showed a different certificate from the one this phone knows. If you made a new one on the PC, scan the code again. If you didn't, don't sign in: something may be pretending to be your PC.
The presented certificate doesn't match the pinned SHA-256. Rescan after a certificate renewal; otherwise treat it as interception.
mobile.help.alerts_body: The owner sets this up once on the PC with a free Firebase key (see the guide on GitHub). Google only carries a nudge with no words in it; the phone then reads the alert from your PC over Tailscale.
The agent sends content-free FCM data messages with a service-account key; the app fetches /api/alerts. Setup: docs/notifications.md.
mobile.help.signout_body: Lost the phone? In the dashboard, open Security and sign it out. The app locks itself out the next time it talks to the PC, and stops getting alerts.
Revoke its session under Security. The next request gets 401 and the app clears its token; its push address is deleted with the session.
mobile.privacy.body: The app talks only to your PC. It keeps your sign-in in the phone's secure storage and sends nothing to us, because there is no us: there is no account, no tracking and no analytics. Lock-screen alerts, if the owner turns them on, go through Google with no words in them. The full privacy policy is on GitHub.

No telemetry, analytics or third-party SDKs besides Firebase Cloud Messaging (only when push alerts are enabled; payloads carry an alert id only). The session token is stored with Android Keystore / iOS Keychain. Full policy: PRIVACY.md.
mobile.error.unreachable: Can't reach your PC. It may be asleep or off, or this phone may not be on Tailscale.
mobile.error.certificate_changed: Your PC showed a different certificate from the one this phone knows. Don't sign in. If you made a new certificate on the PC, scan the code again.
